text: If you lived in Germany for a few years, you can become a permanent resident. As a permanent resident, you can… Live anywhere in Germany Work, study and freelance without the Ausländerbehörde ’s permission Bring your family to Germany Visit other Schengen countries without a visa Become a citizen after 5 years This guide explains how to apply for permanent residence in Berlin.

Permanent residence means more stability. It’s better than a residence permit because… It’s more flexible It’s not tied to your income or occupation. You can change jobs, start a business or study. You don’t need permission from the Ausländerbehörde. It’s permanent You don’t need to renew it every 2 or 3 years. It does not expire if you lose your job. It only expires if you travel outside of Germany for a long time. It’s more trusted It’s easier to open a bank account, get a loan, get a mortgage, or find an apartment as a permanent resident. You might also qualify for German citizenship. Citizenship is better than permanent residence.

title: Basic requirements
text: To become a permanent resident, you must… Support yourself Your income or your spouse’s income must cover your cost of living. [§ 9 Abs. 2 S. 2 AufenthG, Berlin.de (2024)] It must also cover your children and unemployed spouse’s cost of living. [§ 21 Abs. 4 AufenthG] Income from social benefits like Grundsicherung and Sozialhilfe do not count. Income from Kindergeld, Elterngeld, Kinderzuschlag and Erziehungsgeld counts. [§ 2 Abs. 3 AufenthG, § 9 Abs. 2 S. 1 AufenthG, Berlin.de, rtpartner.de] Have a place to live Your apartment must be big enough for you and your family. You need 9 m² per adult, and 6 m² per child. Have health insurance You need public or private health insurance. Expat health insurance and travel insurance are not accepted. Ask my insurance expert to help you choose health insurance. There are more requirements, depending on your situation.

title: If you have a Blue Card
text: To become a permanent resident, you must also… Have a job You must have a stable, long-term income. If you are unemployed, if you are in your probation period, or if your work contract ends in the next 6 months, your application will get rejected. Have a Blue Card for 21 to 27 months 27 months if you speak A1 German, or 21 months if you speak B1 German. [§ 18c Abs. 2 AufenthG, § 2 Abs. 9 and 11 AufenthG, Make it in Germany (June 2024), BAMF (June 2024), Berlin.de] This includes the time when you met the Blue Card requirements, even if you had a different residence permit. Speak A1 or B1 German Pay pension insurance You must pay 27 months of public pension insurance, or 21 months if you speak B1 German. When you are employed, you do this automatically. See the pension requirements.

title: If you have a work visa
text: To become a permanent resident, you must also… Have a § 18a, § 18b or § 18d work visa [§ 18c Abs. 1 AufenthG] The type of work visa is written on your residence permit. If you have a different residence permit, follow the requirements for everybody else. Work for 2 to 3 years [§ 18c Abs. 1 AufenthG] 2 years if you graduated from a German university, 3 years otherwise. This includes the time when you met the work visa requirements, even if you had a different residence permit. Speak B1 German [§ 18c Abs. 1 S. 4 AufenthG] Pay pension insurance You must pay 3 years of pension insurance, or 2 years if you graduated from a German university. When you are employed, you do this automatically. See the pension requirements. If you have a work visa, but you qualify for a Blue Card, you can become a permanent resident in 21 to 27 months. Apply as if you had a Blue Card. See the requirements for Blue Card holders.

title: If you have a freelance visa
text: To become a permanent resident, you must also… Have a § 21 Abs. 1 or 2a freelance visa for 3 years [§ 21 Abs. 4 and 5 AufenthG, Berlin.de, iQ Netzwerk (page 13, 2022)] The type of freelance visa is written on your residence permit. If you have a § 21 Abs. 5 freelance visa, follow the requirements for ev. Have a profitable business You can only get the PR after 3 years if the Ausländerbehörde thinks that your business is successful, profitable and sustainable. Your Ausländerbehörde case worker will decide this. Support yourself In Berlin, they only consider your self-employment income. They ignore income from your spouse and income from investments. In Berlin, if you have a § 21 Abs. 1 or 2a freelance visa, there should be no pension or language requirement. [§ 21 Abs. 4 AufenthG, VAB 21.4.2 (July 2024), Fiona Macdonald, immigration lawyer (June 2024), Twitter (2024)] If you don’t meet those requirements, follow the requirements for everybody else. Then you will need a pension. It might be easier to apply for citizenship, because citizenship does not require a pension.

title: If you live with a German citizen
text: To become a permanent resident, you must also… [§ 28 Abs. 2 AufenthG, Berlin.de (June 2024)] Have a German spouse, child or parent Live together for 3 years You must live together, in Germany, for 3 years without interruption. Speak B1 German There is no pension requirement for the family of German citizens. You can also become a citizen after 3 years.

title: If your spouse is a permanent resident
text: To become a permanent resident, you must also… Live with your spouse for 3 to 5 years 3 years if you work at least 20 hours per week, or 5 years otherwise. [§ 9 Abs. 3a AufenthG, jurati.eu] This includes the time before your spouse became a permanent resident. Your job should not be temporary, and you should not be in your probation period. Self-employment is allowed. Speak B1 German [§ 9 Abs. 3a AufenthG] Your spouse must… Be a permanent resident Be a skilled worker Their last residence permit must have been a Blue Card, or a § 18a, § 18b or § 18d work visa. [§ 9 Abs. 3a AufenthG, § 18c AufenthG] If they had a different residence permit, follow the requirements for everybody else. Have a job They must have a stable, long-term income. If they are unemployed, if they are in their probation period, or if their work contract ends in the next 6 months, your application will be rejected.

title: If you have a student visa
text: You can’t become a permanent resident while on a student visa. Wait until you have a different residence permit like a Blue Card, a work visa or a freelance visa. Your time as a student counts toward your PR, but it’s divided by half. For example, if you studied for 4 years, it counts as 2 years for your PR. [§ 9 Abs. 4 S. 3 AufenthG, jurati.eu (June 2024)]

title: If you are a refugee or asylum seeker
text: To become a permanent resident, you must… [§ 26 Abs. 3 S. 4 AufenthG, jurati.eu] Have the correct residence permit You must have a § 25 Abs. 1, § 25 Abs. 2 S. 1, or § 23 Abs. 4 residence permit. The type is written on your residence permit. If you have a different residence permit, follow the requirements for everybody else. Live in Germany for 3 to 5 years 3 years if you speak C1 German, or 5 years if you speak A2 German. This includes the time when they processed your request for asylum. Speak A2 or C1 German There is no pension requirement for refugees and asylum seekers.

title: For your children
text: To become a permanent resident, your child must… [BAMF, § 35 AufenthG, Berlin.de (July 2024), anwalt-diedrich.de (July 2024)] Be at least 16 years old Live in Germany for 5 years If your child is 16 or 17 years old, they must have lived 5 years in Germany before the age of 16. If your child is 18 years old, they must have lived 5 years in Germany in total. Speak B1 German If your child is 18 years old, they must speak B1 German. If they are 16 or 17 years old, there is no language requirement. Be supported by your income You, your spouse and your child’s income must cover your child’s cost of living. If one parent is a German citizen, your child could get permanent residence in 3 years. If you live with a German citizen

title: Everyone else
text: To become a permanent resident, you must… Live in Germany for 5 years Your time as a student counts, but it’s divided by 2. For example, if you studied for 4 years, it counts as 2 years toward your PR. Speak B1 German [§ 9 Abs. 2 S. 7 AufenthG, § 9a Abs. 2 S. 3 AufenthG] Have a retirement pension You need 60 months of public pension payments, a guaranteed private pension, or equivalent retirement savings. See the pension requirements. If you live 5 years in Germany, you can also become a German citizen. Citizenship is usually better.

title: Pension requirements
text: To get a PR, you need savings for retirement. [§ 9 Abs. 2 S. 3 AufenthG] There are 4 ways to do this: Pay into the public pension system If you are an employee, you automatically pay into the public pension system. If you worked for 60 months, you contributed for 60 months. If you are self-employed or unemployed, you probably don’t make public pension payments. To know how many pension payments you made, get a Versicherungsverlauf. or use your spouse’s pension If you are married, and your spouse has a valid pension, you can use their pension. For example, if your spouse has made 60 months of public pension payments, it’s enough. [BAMF (June 2024), rtpartner.de, § 9 Abs. 3 S. 1 AufenthG, VAB 9.2.1.3.3 (July 2024)] or get a private pension It must guarantee an income of at least € 1,612.53 per month for at least 12 years after you retire. It must include a pension in case of disability. A Rürüp pension like the one Feather sells should work fine. or use your foreign pension A guaranteed pension from another country also counts. or have real estate or other investments Stable income from your investments might replace a pension. There is no clear information about this. In Berlin, you need a guaranteed pension. Stocks or money in your bank account are not enough. Investments that bring a stable income might be enough. There is no clear information about this. If you are self-employed, you don’t pay for a public pension. Instead, you can… Make voluntary public pension payments You can make the minimum contribution (€ 111.97 per month) until you have 60 months of pension contributions. To make voluntary contributions, fill form V0060. You can make retroactive payments for up to 1 year. or join the Künstlersozialkasse If you are a freelance artist, publicist or teacher, the KSK can pay half of your pension. It’s a cheaper way to get a pension. or use your foreign pension You can use your pension from Australia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Brazil, Canada, Chile, India, Israel, Japan, Kosovo, Morocco, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia, South Korea, Tunisia, Turkey or the United States. You might need to get a proof of your foreign pension from the Deutsche Rentenversicherung. or get a private pension or use your spouse’s pension or have enough savings It looks like you need at least € 232,204 in savings. There is no clear information about this. It might not work. If you try it, let me know. If you are a refugee or an asylum seeker, you don’t need a pension. If you don’t have a pension, you can become a German citizen instead. There is no pension requirement for citizenship.

title: Citizenship
text: If you can’t get permanent residence, you might still qualify for German citizenship. To become a German citizen, you must… Live in Germany for 5 years, or 3 years if you have a German spouse [§ 9 Abs. 1 StAG] Speak B1 German [§ 10 Abs. 1 S. 6 StAG, BMI (June 2024)] Support yourself and your family, without using social benefits Take the citizenship test ( Einbürgerungstest) Not be convicted of a crime Citizenship is better than permanent residence because… You get a German passport You can live and work in other EU countries without a residence permit You can’t lose your citizenship Your citizenship does not expire if you leave Germany for over 6 months You don’t need a pension to qualify If your country does not allow dual citizenship, becoming a German citizen means losing your old citizenship. In this case, permanent residence might be a better option. For example, China and India don’t allow dual citizenship.

title: EU Permanent Residence
text: There are two types of permanent residence: German permanent residence ( Niederlassungserlaubnis) and EU permanent residence ( Daueraufenthalt-EU). They are almost the same. EU permanent residence is a little better because… You can leave Germany for a longer period German PR expires after 6 months outside of Germany. EU permanent residence expires after 12 to 24 months outside the EU, or 6 years in another EU country. [§ 51 Abs. 2 AufenthG, se-legal.de (July 2024), Berlin.de (July 2024), Hamburg (July 2024)] It’s easier to move to another EU country With the EU PR, you can move to another country, then apply for a residence permit there. With the German PR, you might need to apply for a residence permit at the embassy in Germany, then move to that country. You can only get an EU PR after 5 years in Germany. You can sometimes get a German PR faster. The requirements and the application process are the same. If you qualify for the EU PR, you get the EU PR. Usually, if you lived in Germany for 5 years, you get the EU PR.

In Berlin, you must apply online. It takes 3 to 7 months to get permanent residence. If you don’t live in Berlin, you must find your local Ausländerbehörde and follow their instructions. The application process can be different. If you need help, an immigration lawyer or a relocation consultant can take care of everything. It costs € 500 to € 2,000.

title: 1. Take an integration test
text: You need a certificate from… The citizenship test ( Einbürgerungstest) You must book an appointment. Then you go to your appointment in person to book a test date. The test costs € 25. It has 33 questions, multiple choice. In Berlin, it’s really hard to get an appointment because there are no free slots. It can be faster to take the test in another city. or the Leben in Deutschland test This is the same test and the same questions. You usually take that test after an integration course at the Volkshochschule. The course is very boring. You can take the test without taking the course, but only if they have free slots. In Berlin, this could be really hard. After you take the test, it takes 2 to 8 weeks to get the results. If you graduated from a German high school or university, you don’t need this test. You must have studied in German, not English.

title: 2. Prepare your application
text: Before you apply for permanent residence, prepare your documents. If you are self-employed, some documents must be prepared by a tax advisor. It can be hard to find a tax advisor. It can take a few weeks to prepare the documents. Required documents

title: 3. Apply for permanent residence online
text: You must apply for the permanent residence online. You do not need an Ausländerbehörde appointment. Apply for permanent residence It costs € 100. It’s cheaper for Turkish citizens. You can pay with Visa, Mastercard or PayPal. You can’t pay with cash or Girocard. The application fee is not tax-deductible. If you have too many documents, merge them or make them smaller. After you pay and send your application, you can download a PDF. This is your proof of application. Save it for later.

title: 4. Wait
text: The Ausländerbehörde will process your application. It takes 3 to 7 months. You must wait for their response. There is no way to track your application. If you wait more than 3 months, you can sue the Ausländerbehörde. While you wait, your current National Visa or residence permit might expire. It’s extended until the Ausländerbehörde processes your application. [§ 81 Abs. 5 AufenthG] What happens while you wait

title: 5. Go to your appointment
text: A few months later, the Ausländerbehörde will email you an appointment date. If you get an appointment, you are almost guaranteed to get your permanent residence. Follow the instructions in the email. You might need to send extra documents, or bring them to your appointment. They usually ask for more recent proof of income, employment, health insurance and rent payments. Print them and bring them. The appointment takes around 15 minutes. They ask you questions in German about your height, your eye colour, how long you have been in Germany, if you like living in Berlin, and the size of your apartment. What happens during your appointment If your permanent residence is approved, you will get another appointment to pick up your plastic residence card.

title: 6. Get your permanent residence card
text: Go to your second Ausländerbehörde appointment and pick up your permanent residence card. How to pick up your permanent residence card Tell us how long it took to apply for a residence permit in Berlin. This tool requires JavaScript to work.

These are the required documents in Berlin. In other cities, you need different documents. Check the website of the Ausländerbehörde where you apply. When you apply online, use PDF files or photos. Don’t use word documents or other formats. If you have too many documents, merge them or make them smaller. You can also mail your documents, but it’s not better or faster. Applications by email are usually ignored. When you go to your appointment, bring the documents that they ask for in your appointment confirmation. Put dates on all your documents. Print everything on A4 paper. Do not staple the pages together. Some case workers also ask for documents that you already sent. It’s safer if you bring everything you have, including documents that you already sent.

title: Required documents for everyone
text: Passport When you apply online, include a colour scan of your passport. When you go to your appointment, bring your original passport. You get it back during the appointment; they do not keep it. Language certificate You need a language certificate from an approved school (telc or Goethe). The required language level ( A1, A2, B1 or C1) depends on your situation. If you studied in German at a German university, you don’t need a language certificate. Proof of integration You need a certificate from one of these courses: Citizenship test ( Einbürgerungstest) or “Leben in Deutschland” test or integration course ( Integrationskurs) Citizenship test ( Einbürgerungstest) or “Leben in Deutschland” test or integration course ( Integrationskurs) Proof of health insurance You need valid health insurance. Travel insurance is not accepted. Health insurance card Show both sides of the card. proof of public health insurance Get a Mitgliedsbescheinigung nach § 175 SGB V from your health insurer or your health insurance broker. proof of private health insurance Bring your insurance contract, a Mitgliedsbescheinigung nach § 257 SGB V, and bank statements that show health insurance payments. Get these documents from your health insurer or your health insurance broker. [§ 21 Abs. 4 and 5 AufenthG, Berlin.de, iQ Netzwerk (page 13, 2022)] Health insurance card Show both sides of the card. proof of public health insurance Get a Mitgliedsbescheinigung nach § 175 SGB V from your health insurer or your health insurance broker. proof of private health insurance Bring your insurance contract, a Mitgliedsbescheinigung nach § 257 SGB V, and bank statements that show health insurance payments. Get these documents from your health insurer or your health insurance broker. [§ 21 Abs. 4 and 5 AufenthG, Berlin.de, iQ Netzwerk (page 13, 2022)] Proof of health insurance payments Bring bank account statements that show recent health insurance payments. Proof of housing You need a place to live where you can register your address. If you apply in Berlin, your home address must be in Berlin. Lease Bring the original, not a copy. It must show the size of your apartment. Your apartment must be big enough (9 m² per adult, 6 m² per child). You must make enough money to pay your rent. It can be a temporary lease, a WG, a sublet or a student residence. and tenancy confirmation ( Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) Some temporary apartments and sublets don’t give you this document. You might not get a PR without it. Bring it even if you registered your address. and registration certificate ( Anmeldebestätigung) and proof of rent payments Print recent bank statements that show rent payments. Lease Bring the original, not a copy. It must show the size of your apartment. Your apartment must be big enough (9 m² per adult, 6 m² per child). You must make enough money to pay your rent. It can be a temporary lease, a WG, a sublet or a student residence. and tenancy confirmation ( Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) Some temporary apartments and sublets don’t give you this document. You might not get a PR without it. Bring it even if you registered your address. and registration certificate ( Anmeldebestätigung) and proof of rent payments Print recent bank statements that show rent payments. Proof of pension See the pension requirements. Versicherungsverlauf from the Deutsche Rentenversicherung Request a Versicherungsverlauf online. It arrives by post in 1 to 3 weeks. If you have an eID, you can get a Versicherungsverlauf instantly. or proof of private pension Bring your pension contract, and bank account statements that show pension payments. Versicherungsverlauf from the Deutsche Rentenversicherung Request a Versicherungsverlauf online. It arrives by post in 1 to 3 weeks. If you have an eID, you can get a Versicherungsverlauf instantly. or proof of private pension Bring your pension contract, and bank account statements that show pension payments. Translations If your documents are not in German, bring translations. For certificates and official documents, bring certified translations. They sometimes accept untranslated documents, but don’t take the risk. Get translations from Red Tape Translation or Lingoking. If you receive social benefits like Kindergeld, Kinderzuschlag, Elterngeld, Betreuungsgeld, you must bring… Proof of social benefits Bring certificates and other documents that prove that you receive those social benefits.

title: For employees
text: Work contract ( Arbeitsvertrag) Recent pay slips ( Gehaltsabrechnung) Bring your pay slips for the last 6 months. Employment certificate ( Arbeitgeberbescheinigung) It must be less than 14 days old. Get it from your employer. Required documents for Blue Card holders Required documents for work visa holders

title: For self-employed people
text: Proof of income Audit report form ( Prüfungsbericht) Your tax advisor must fill this template and stamp it. It takes a few days to prepare. If your finances are not organised, it can take a few weeks. If you don’t have a tax advisor, get a Prüfungsbericht from Tax Germany; it’s cheaper and faster. Income tax assessment ( Steuerbescheid) If you don’t have it yet, bring a Netto-Gewinnermittlung. It’s not in the required documents, but they usually ask for it. Net profit assessment ( Netto-Gewinnermittlung) If you don’t have a recent tax return, bring this instead. This document must be stamped by a tax advisor. If you don’t have a tax advisor, get it from Tax Germany. It takes a few days to prepare. Audit report form ( Prüfungsbericht) Your tax advisor must fill this template and stamp it. It takes a few days to prepare. If your finances are not organised, it can take a few weeks. If you don’t have a tax advisor, get a Prüfungsbericht from Tax Germany; it’s cheaper and faster. Income tax assessment ( Steuerbescheid) If you don’t have it yet, bring a Netto-Gewinnermittlung. It’s not in the required documents, but they usually ask for it. Net profit assessment ( Netto-Gewinnermittlung) If you don’t have a recent tax return, bring this instead. This document must be stamped by a tax advisor. If you don’t have a tax advisor, get it from Tax Germany. It takes a few days to prepare. Certificate of tax matters ( Bescheinigung in Steuersachen) It proves that you paid your taxes on time. Request it from the Finanzamt. It costs € 17.90. It arrives in 1 to 3 weeks. Trade certificate ( Gewerbeschein) If your business is a Gewerbe, bring your Gewerbeschein. If you are a Freiberufler, you don’t need this. Trade register entry ( Handelsregisterauszug) If you need a Handelsregister entry, bring a Handelsregisterauszug. Required documents for self-employed people

title: For spouses of German citizens
text: If you depend on your spouse’s income, bring… Your spouse’s work contract ( Arbeitsvertrag) Their recent pay slips ( Gehaltsabrechnung) Bring their pay slips for the last 6 months. Their employment certificate ( Arbeitgeberbescheinigung) It must be less than 14 days old. Get it from their employer. Required documents for spouses

title: Activate your eID
text: You can use your permanent residence card to log into online government services. If you pick up your card at the Ausländerbehörde, it should already be activated. Make sure it works before you really need it. How to activate your eID

title: Travel as a permanent resident
text: With a PR, you can visit other Schengen area countries without a visa. If you have German permanent residence, you can travel 6 months outside of Germany. If you have EU permanent residence, you can travel 12 to 24 months outside the EU, or 6 years in another EU country. [§ 51 Abs. 2 AufenthG, se-legal.de (July 2024), Berlin.de (July 2024), Hamburg (July 2024)] Travel with a residence permit

title: Renew your permanent residence
text: When you get a new passport, your permanent residence card becomes invalid. You are still a permanent resident, but you must get a new card. To get a new card, get a Bürgeramt appointment, go in person, pay € 67, and wait a few weeks. [ArbeitNow (2023), § 45c AufenthV] You should get the card by post. The eID function might be deactivated on your new card. You might need another Bürgeramt appointment to activate it.
An immigration lawyer or a relocation consultant can answer your questions. Some organisations can also help you for free. Where to ask immigration questions
